blocks.text: Bread, *çörek*, is on the cloth at almost every Turkmen meal. The everyday loaf is round, flat on top and thick, and it is baked in a *tamdyr*, a clay oven shaped like a dome or a big jar, often built in the courtyard of a house.

Making a tamdyr is a craft of its own. Clay is kneaded with straw, and sometimes with sheep or camel wool, so that the oven keeps its heat and doesn't crack. Before baking, wood burns inside it for a long time. Then the baker slaps the rounds of dough against the hot inner wall, where they stick and bake in minutes, and lifts them out with a metal hook. Loaves are often pricked with a pattern of dots before they go in.

There is more than one kind of bread. *Ýagly çörek* is flaky and layered with butter or fat; *etli çörek* has meat baked inside and makes a meal on its own; *petir* is a thin flat bread. Older Turkmens told the food writer Darra Goldstein that the national cooking once had more than a hundred kinds of filled breads, and some lost recipes are coming back. Bread also goes into dishes: for *dograma*, bread is torn by hand into small pieces and mixed with meat and hot broth.

Bread is treated with great respect. It is impolite to put a loaf upside down or to treat bread carelessly, and there are many customs and sayings around it and around the oven. Bread is usually broken by hand and shared, and it comes to the table with green tea, which you met in [A1 unit 6](a1-u06-culture).

In towns many families now buy their bread at the market or the bakery; a public bakery in Ashgabat described in 2006 baked in half a dozen of these ovens, fired with natural gas. Still, the clay oven in the yard has not disappeared, in villages or in towns.

blocks.title: Bread and this unit
blocks.text: *çörek* shows this unit's sound change: *çörek alýaryn* (I'm buying bread), but *çöregi alýaryn* (I'm buying the bread), with *k* → *g* before the vowel.
With the words of this unit, you can read this:

blocks.tk: Biz bazardan çörek alýarys. Çörek gyzgyn! Men çöregi stola goýýaryn. Myhmanlar çaý içýärler we çörek iýýärler.
blocks.en: We buy bread at the market. The bread is hot! I put the bread on the table. The guests drink tea and eat bread.

questions.q: Why is it *çöregi* in *Men çöregi stola goýýaryn*?
options: It is a particular bread, the object, and *k* becomes *g* before a vowel
questions.explain: **The** bread takes the object ending, and the *k* of *çörek* softens before it.
